translation_notes: Every next(graph.objects(subject=..., predicate=...), None) becomes m{ }.first(); the loop over graph.objects(...) becomes a bare `for x in m{ }`.

AAS predicates are e.g. AASNameSpace.AAS["Referable/category"], a local part with a slash -- not a legal Turtle prefixed name. Used @base <https://admin-shell.io/aas/3/0/> . and wrote each predicate as a relative <Referable/category> IRI rather than a prefixed name, since PN_LOCAL cannot carry an unescaped '/'.

shim.py supplies minimal pydantic stand-ins for AASNameSpace/HasExtensions/Referable/LangString*Type (the real ones live in app.models, unreachable outside the package); HasExtensions.from_rdf keeps its own one-step read, exercised by the fixture's zero-extensions case.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the four copies of `x_ref = next(graph.objects(...), None); x_value = None; if x_ref: x_value = x_ref.value` collapse into one local helper `value(node, local_name)` (`ref = graph.value(node, AASNameSpace.AAS[local_name])`, `return ref.value if ref else None`), and the two identical display-name / description loops into one helper `lang_strings(local_name, lang_string_type)`, a list comprehension ending in `or None` (the `if len(...) == 0: ... = None` guard). The Referable(...) call takes the values directly. `graph.value(s, p)` is `next(graph.objects(s, p), None)` for a non-None subject; `subject` is typed IdentifiedNode and the inner nodes come from graph.objects(), so never None.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `AASNameSpace.AAS[local_name]` becomes `f<{local_name}>`, resolved against the header's `@base <https://admin-shell.io/aas/3/0/>`; the helpers and their call sites are otherwise identical.

Rule 4: `m{ {node} f<{local_name}> ?o }.first()` and `m{ {subject} f<{local_name}> ?o }` with `@graph graph` were measured at 168 tokens against 165 for `graph.value(node, f<{local_name}>)` / `graph.objects(subject, f<{local_name}>)`, so the rdflib calls are kept and only the IRI notation is used.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
